title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a linear-algebra and derived-category model for the Dieudonné theory of level-1 truncated Barsotti–Tate groups (BT_1), or more generally finite flat group schemes killed by p, over an arbitrary base S of characteristic p. It is the abstract skeleton of the programme stated on the next page: attach to G/S a Dieudonné crystal D*(G), co-Lie complexes l_G and l_{G*}, and a triangle on S_cris that determines D*_cris(G).

(a) Crystalline side. Let M be a crystal on (S/F_p)_cris, 'locally free annihilated by p' (locally free over O_cris/p), with F: M^(p) → M and V: M → M^(p), and FV = VF = p. Since p kills M, FV = VF = 0. From M one builds perfect crystalline complexes:
- L(M) = [M^(p) --F--> M], labelled 'Frob';
- L^!(M) = [M --V--> M^(p)], labelled 'Versch';
- Δ(M), of perfect amplitude in [0,1], with H^0(Δ) ≅ H^1(Δ) ≅ M.
One natural reading is Δ = RHom(Z/p, M) = [M --p=0--> M], or RHom(G, O_cris ⊗^L Z/p) for G killed by p. Δ carries F_Δ and V_Δ with F_Δ V_Δ = 0 and V_Δ F_Δ = 0.

Two exact triangles relate these:
- (I)_cris: [M^(p) → M] → Δ^(p) → [M → M^(p)] → +1;
- (II)_cris: [M → M^(p)] → Δ → [M^(p) → M] → +1.
The boxed NB says all three are (F,V)-complexes and that (I) and (II) are compatible with the (F,V)-structures. On cohomology, these triangles encode the BT_1 exactness ker F = im V and ker V = im F. This exactness is what makes H^0(Δ) an extension of the two kernels.

The key device is a morphism of topoi φ: (S/F_p)_cris → S_zar with Δ^(p) ≅ φ*(ε*Δ). Here ε* is restriction to the Zariski site. The point is that for a PD-thickening killed by p, Frobenius factors through the thickening. So the Frobenius pullback F_S^*E of any O_S-module E is canonically a crystal. Hence the Frobenius twist of a crystal depends only on its Zariski restriction.

(b) Zariski side. Take perfect complexes l and l^! on S_zar of amplitude [-1,0], meant to be the co-Lie complexes l_G and l_{G*}. Take a Zariski triangle (III): l[-1] --i0--> ε*Δ --π0--> (l^!)^∨ --∂0--> l. Require isomorphisms φ*(l[-1]) ≅ [M^(p) --F--> M] and φ*((l^!)^∨) ≅ [M --V--> M^(p)], identifying (I)_cris with φ*(III).

Consequence (bracketed remark, with '!'). Put M = ε*M, a locally free O_S-module with integrable connection. Then:
- l[-1]^(p) ≅ [M^(p) --F_M--> M];
- (l^!)^∨(p) ≅ [M --V_M--> M^(p)];
- both compatibly with the connection.
So the Frobenius twist of the co-Lie (Hodge) data is computed by the F- and V-complexes of the Dieudonné module. This is the derived form of 'Frobenius-twisted Hodge filtration = conjugate filtration = im V = ker F'.

Compatibility (last lines). Grothendieck proposes to define Frobenius and Verschiebung on the co-Lie complexes by composites of triangle maps:
- F_{l^!} := π0 ∘ ε*(i_II), which equals the transpose of V_{l^!};
- V_{l[-1]} := ε*(π_II) ∘ i0.
The page stops there: the axiomatics is set up but no theorem is proved.
errors: No real error. 'FV = VF = p' for a crystal annihilated by p just means FV = VF = 0, which is how it is used for Δ.

The Frobenius twist appears on Δ in (I) but not in (II). This is consistent only via the identification Δ^(p) ≅ φ*(ε*Δ). The exact orientation of the extension (sub ker F, quotient ker V versus the natural filtration of M) is not checked on the page; signs and shifts of the degree-1 maps ∂ are left implicit.

Several items are marked '?' (locally free of finite type? perfect amplitude?), and the compatibility conditions are only stated with scare-quoted equalities. This is a sketch, not a verified construction.

ideas.what: Dieudonné crystal of a group killed by p as a locally free crystal over O_cris/p with F, V, FV = VF = 0 and the exactness ker F = im V, ker V = im F
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné crystal of a BT_1 / truncated Dieudonné crystal; related to F-zips

ideas.what: Derived Dieudonné object Δ(M), a perfect 2-term crystalline complex with H^0 ≅ H^1 ≅ M, sitting in two (F,V)-compatible triangles with the F-complex and V-complex
ideas.modern_name: M ⊗^L Z/p, or RHom(G, O_cris ⊗^L Z/p); derived/complex-level Dieudonné theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution in this form; derived Dieudonné ideas in Illusie 1985 and later Bhatt–Lurie (F-gauges)

missed.claim: Proposed classification datum for groups killed by p over arbitrary bases: a crystal M with F, V, together with Zariski co-Lie complexes l, l^! and a triangle (III) whose Frobenius-twisted crystalline pullback is identified with the canonical (F,V)-triangle on Δ(M). This is formulated at the level of perfect complexes, so it would include non-smooth or non-flat-Lie situations. The equivalence or full-faithfulness of this datum is never stated or proved.
missed.quote: fournissant un isom de (I_cris) avec φ*(III)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a derived 'F-zip with Hodge complexes' for BT_1 or p-torsion groups over general bases, close in spirit to Bhatt–Lurie syntomic/F-gauge Dieudonné theory and to Lau's work on Dieudonné theory for p-torsion groups; it could be compared with those classifications.

missed.claim: The remark that the Frobenius twist of the co-Lie complex is quasi-isomorphic to the F-complex [M^(p) → M], horizontally for the connection, is the complex-level version of the F-zip identity (Hodge filtration twisted equals conjugate filtration).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates Moonen–Wedhorn F-zips (2004) and their derived/gauge refinements, and shows Grothendieck was thinking in derived terms about the Hodge versus conjugate structure around 1970.

missed.claim: Use of a morphism of topoi φ from the crystalline topos to the Zariski topos realizing Frobenius pullback as a crystal, predating the standard published treatments by Berthelot–Ogus.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical credit; the device is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The general programme (Dieudonné crystals plus co-Lie complexes for BT groups over arbitrary bases) is known from Grothendieck's Montreal notes and from Illusie. What is less known is the specific derived formulation: the 2-term complex Δ with H^0 = H^1 = M, the paired F- and V-triangles, the Frobenius-twisted descent to Zariski co-Lie complexes, and the horizontal 'Hodge^(p) = F-complex' remark. Together these anticipate F-zips and derived/gauge approaches, but the page is a sketch without results.
transcription_corrections: First line: probably '[Cristaux] p-is.. (loc. libres annulés par p en car. p)', i.e. 'en car p' rather than 'ou ≠ p'.
In the NB box the superscripts after the complexes read like degree markers '[01]' and '[10]' (degrees of the two terms), not '[0]' and '[1]'.

Next to (I) the image reads 'Δ*^(p) ≃ φ*(Δ*)' with '(Δ* = ε*(Δ*))' beneath, where the right-hand Δ is the crystalline object. φ is a crystalline-to-Zariski morphism of topoi, not a pullback of a crystal.
In b) the word 'Rem' before '[d'où' is a bracket mark, probably just 'Rq' or a bracket. A margin note 'compat. avec connexion' accompanies the two isomorphisms.
In the compatibility lines, 'Posons' is written above the brace.
